front.title: Right Before Action (REHT): Execution-Time Authorization for AI-Mediated Actions

abstract.t: This document defines REHT, a protocol pattern for making fresh organizational authority an executable precondition for a consequence-bearing action. REHT is evaluated at the execution boundary, binds the exact candidate action to current authority and governed state, fails closed on revocation, replay, drift, or unresolved required authority state, and produces integrity-bindable evidence of the verification. REHT does not define an agent runtime, policy engine, identity system, payment rail, or global ordering service.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: AI-mediated systems increasingly separate reasoning from consequence. An agent may prepare an action substantially earlier than the point at which a payment is committed, a production configuration is changed, a record is disclosed, or another irreversible or material effect is created. A prior approval, credential, capability, or successful evaluation is therefore insufficient if authority, scope, state, or revocation status can change before consequence.

REHT places a fresh authorization verification in the consequence path. The central invariant is that the exact candidate action MUST still be within current organizational authority immediately before consequence. Authorization is not treated as a durable bearer fact.

REHT makes fresh organizational authority an executable precondition for irreversible or otherwise consequence-bearing action. It does not claim to be the only protocol capable of enforcing such a property.

section.name: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

dl.dd: The exact consequence-bearing action proposed for execution.
State whose current standing is established by the governing organization or an independently trusted source for the relevant authority decision.
The fresh execution-boundary evaluation that determines whether the exact Candidate Action remains within current authority.

Policy Enforcement Point. The component that prevents an effect unless the required REHT verification and any bound deterministic execution decision permit progression. The PEP does not originate organizational authority.
A deterministic decision and action-binding contract used by the VALO reference profile. RACS does not evaluate or originate authority.

section.name: Protocol Invariants
section.t: A conforming implementation MUST preserve all of the following:

ol.li: REHT MUST verify current authority for the exact Candidate Action at the execution boundary.
A prior approval, clearance, capability, credential, or unexpired validity interval MUST NOT by itself establish current execution authority.
Revocation or material authority drift that is causally prior to the consequence MUST invalidate reliance on an earlier authorization.
Delegated authority MUST NOT widen the capability, scope, purpose, constraints, or validity of its parent authority.
A materially changed action MUST be treated as a new Candidate Action and MUST receive fresh REHT verification.
Single-use execution identities, nonces, permits, or equivalent bindings MUST be replay-resistant.
Missing or unresolved required authority state MUST fail closed.
The effect path MUST NOT permit a worker, agent, orchestrator, or connector to bypass the required execution-boundary verification.

section.name: Trust Boundary
section.t: Agent-produced plans, action traces, memories, tool histories, and self-attestations are inputs. They are not authoritative state merely because an agent signed or produced them.

A trace signature may establish integrity and attribution of the agent's claim. It MUST NOT be interpreted as proof that the claimed authority, organizational mandate, external state, or effect is true.

A REHT verifier SHOULD obtain execution-relevant authority and revocation state independently of worker-controlled assertions where practical. Where a governed context materializes that state on the verifier's behalf, provenance, freshness, and continuity MUST remain independently verifiable.

section.name: Commit Request
section.t: A Commit Request asks REHT to determine whether one exact Candidate Action is currently authorized. Implementations MAY encode the request differently, but an interoperable representation MUST bind at least the following semantics.

The action_digest MUST deterministically bind all consequence-bearing fields whose change could alter the meaning or effect of the Candidate Action. A verifier MUST NOT authorize a materially different action under the same digest binding.

section.name: Commit-Time Verification
section.t: Upon receiving a Commit Request, the REHT verifier MUST perform the execution-boundary verification using current authoritative state. At minimum, where applicable, the verifier MUST establish:

ol.li: the execution identity and actor binding;
the current authority grant and required capability;
the current purpose binding when purpose is required;
required evidence whose absence is material to authorization.

section.t: If a relevant revocation is current or causally prior to consequence, REHT MUST refuse execution under the earlier authority. The PEP MUST enforce that result, but the PEP does not become the source or evaluator of organizational authority merely by enforcing it.

A conforming deployment MUST position REHT verification in the actual commit path. If a relevant authority mutation can intervene between verification and effect, the deployment MUST re-establish current authorization before the effect or provide an equivalent atomic or causally bound mechanism. It MUST NOT rely on a stale cached result.

section.name: Commit Result
section.t: The protocol-level Commit Result expresses whether the exact Candidate Action passed the current REHT verification. It does not redefine a downstream decision vocabulary such as RACS.

An authorized value of true is scoped only to the exact bound action and current verification context. It MUST NOT be treated as durable authority for a later materially changed action or after a causally prior revocation or authority mutation.

When authorization cannot be established, authorized MUST be false and the implementation SHOULD return stable reason codes suitable for deterministic downstream handling. A missing or malformed result MUST fail closed.

section.name: RACS Composition Profile
section.t: RACS is not the protocol-level authorization vocabulary defined by this document. When a deployment composes REHT with the canonical RACS v0.2 decision contract, the RACS decision value MUST be exactly one of:

RACS MAY preserve or narrow a verified REHT result according to its deterministic contract. RACS MUST NOT expand authority. In particular, a failed REHT verification MUST NOT be transformed into ALLOW or otherwise made executable by RACS.

A MODIFY result denotes a constrained or replacement candidate according to the applicable RACS contract; any material change to the consequence-bearing action MUST return to fresh REHT verification before consequence.

section.name: PEP Enforcement
section.t: The PEP is the governed effect boundary. It MUST prevent consequence unless the exact action presented for execution is bound to a current successful REHT verification and all required deterministic execution bindings permit progression.

The PEP MUST reject replay, action-digest mismatch, missing required bindings, malformed verification evidence, and any result that is not executable under the deployed profile. It MUST NOT infer authority from tool possession, credentials, agent claims, schema validity, or execution success.

section.name: Evidence and Ordering
section.t: REHT evidence MUST preserve enough information to reconstruct the Candidate Action, the verification result, the relevant authority state reference, and the consequence or refusal that followed.

This document does not require or claim a global total order across independently owned systems. A conforming evidence record MAY use an issuer-local monotonic sequence together with a parent hash or other causal linkage.

Wall-clock timestamps MAY be retained for policy, correlation, operations, audit, and forensics. They MUST NOT be treated as a substitute for current authority or causal continuity where either is required.

section.name: Credential and Identity Composition
section.t: REHT does not define a mandatory identity or credential format. Deployments MAY compose REHT with W3C Verifiable Credentials or other identity and authority representations. Possession or validation of a credential does not by itself establish that the exact action remains authorized at consequence time; current scope, revocation, constraints, and applicable governed state still require verification.

section.name: Failure Behavior
section.t: A conforming implementation MUST fail closed when a required input is missing, malformed, stale, unverifiable, revoked, materially mismatched, replayed, or known to be unresolved.
Transport failure, verifier unavailability, evidence-store failure, revocation-registry failure, or inability to prove required current authority MUST NOT silently degrade into authorization.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: The principal security objective is to prevent stale, replayed, widened, or self-asserted authority from crossing the consequence boundary. Implementations therefore need integrity protection for action bindings and verification records, replay protection, current revocation handling, strict separation between agent claims and authoritative state, and a governed effect path that cannot be bypassed by the worker that proposed the action.

Cryptographic integrity and signer identity are separate from signer authority and external truth. A valid signature MUST NOT be treated as proof that the signer had organizational authority, that a claimed state was current, or that an external consequence occurred correctly.

Implementations SHOULD minimize sensitive authority-state disclosure. A verifier can expose stable references and digests needed for conformance and audit without disclosing the complete underlying organizational policy or state to the worker.

section.name: Privacy Considerations
section.t: Execution-authorization evidence can reveal organizational structure, identities, targets, purposes, and sensitive action details. Implementations SHOULD minimize exported fields, use opaque references where sufficient, restrict evidence access, and avoid retaining agent traces or personal data that are not required for authorization, dispute resolution, audit, or applicable legal obligations.
